User priorities (20 Nov): better use of the large first-week revision, NHSN hospital reporting coverage, covariates, ideas from well-performing Hub models; avoid overfitting small differences.
history: docs/experiments/flusight-revisions-nowcast-20261120: the CDC evaluation of 18 Nov ranks ACCIDDA-Chromantis 12th over the season (tied with FluSight-ensemble) and 47th over the last two target weeks, mostly from Bes's 7 Nov over-forecast. Nowcasting costs B7 about 5% of WIS at every horizon and Bes nothing; B7 stays 17-18% low at horizons 2-3 even with later inputs (growth forecast). Flu nowcast-tree-20261113 round 1 (B_width256 family, 2024-25 and 2025-26 held out, error_reference=2025-2026, seeds 44-47): trees from real report pairs 0.299 vs 0.313 for Bes as submitted; reading hospital coverage did not help the forecast (0.303). The COVID/RSV coverage search (experiments/covid-rsv-coverage-20261118) found US-only summary exchange (RSV), a GRU encoder and log-loss weight 1 (COVID) helpful, and that networks trained on uncorrected histories with final-value labels count the tree correction twice.
first_week_signal: scripts/flu_first_week_signal.py (20 Nov, Longleaf, panel-coverage.npz): for the newest reported week of each state (>= 5 admissions) in 2024-25 and 2025-26, the log revision to the value 12 weeks later (mean +0.065 / +0.074) is predicted out of season by the hospital-coverage ratio (hospitals reporting that week / median of weeks t-5..t-3; R2 0.24 testing on 2024-25, 0.40 on 2025-26), not by the revision observed last week between a week's first and second report (R2 0.00-0.05) nor by the state's past first-week revisions (0.00). Adding them to coverage gives no gain. So the first-week revision is best used through coverage, which the trees already read; no new feature was coded.
hub_ideas: Hub models with the lowest pairwise relative log WIS in 2024-25 / 2025-26 (from the planner's Hub comparison): FluSight-trained_mean, FluSight-ensemble, PSI-PROF_beta, UMass-flusion, CMU-TimeSeries / Google_SAI-FluEns, OHT_JHU-nbxd, CMU-TimeSeries, UGA_flucast-INFLAenza. Their metadata: ensembles of structurally different models (Google, CU, CMU, UMass, JHU), training augmented with historical ILINet and FluSurv-NET rescaled to admissions (CMU, CU, UMass), averaging over several lookback windows and initializations (JHU), fourth-root scale and AR terms (UMass), lab positivity (JHU). Tested here as: ILI pretraining, FluSurv-NET/ILINet/clinical-lab covariates, lookback children, fourth-root/sqrt transforms, and mixtures of different recipes and lookbacks.

problems.main: problems/us-flu-short-term-coverage.json: 2024-25 and 2025-26 each held out in turn, training on the other seasons of 2022-23..2025-26 (so the 2024-25 fold also trains on the later 2025-26), labels = finalized future values, evaluated on the held-out season's archived Wednesday reports (finalized values where nothing was archived).
problems.guard: problems/us-flu-2023-24-prescribed-coverage.json (new): 2023-24 held out, training on 2022-23, 2024-25 and 2025-26, evaluated on artificial preliminary 2023-24 reports (2025-26 reporting errors on admissions, ED and covariates, 3 draws). A third epidemic, never used to select flu models before; its reports are artificial, so it guards the growth forecast more than the nowcast.

leak_free_errors: Change from every earlier flu study: recipes carry no error_reference in the main problem, so each fold draws its artificial reporting errors and real report pairs from its own latest training season (2024-25 errors for the 2025-26 fold, 2025-26 errors for the 2024-25 fold). Before, error_reference=2025-2026 trained the 2025-26 fold on 2025-26's own reporting errors, which flatters recipes that rely on artificial errors when 2025-26 is scored. The guard needs a named reference and uses error_reference=2025-2026 (its default donor too). Scores are therefore not comparable with nowcast-tree-20261113.

families.ref: B7's members as submitted except for leak-free errors: ref.A (A_blocks3: width-96 sampled MLP, three-block decoder, Kinsa, network on tree-corrected histories), ref.B5 (B5_confirmed_candidate_1: width-96 sampled MLP, pre-2022 ILI pretraining, multiscale features, Kinsa), ref.B (B_width256: width-256 direct-quantile MLP, neighbouring states, network on uncorrected artificial histories plus final-value labels of the last 4 weeks), ref.Bes (ref.B with errors at 1.5x).
families.roots: Bq = ref.B with trees learned from real archived report -> value 12 weeks later pairs. Bh = ref.B's network trained on tree-corrected histories instead of final-value labels (no double correction), trees from real pairs, trees and network reading hospital coverage, coverage errors drawn with the admission errors. Ar = ref.A with real-pair trees.
families.children: One change each (experiments/flu-search-20261120/rounds.py): nat (US-only summary instead of neighbours), gru, ll1 (log-loss weight 1), lb8/lb16 (lookback), ili (pre-2022 ILI pretraining), cw1 (trees correct the newest week only), esall (errors and pairs from every archived season), act50 (half the training episodes from actual archived reports), cov / netcov0 (coverage read by trees and network / trees only), clab, fsurv, ilinet, ww, kinsa / nokinsa (covariates), tr (sqrt <-> fourth root), noise (sampled out-of-fold nowcast errors, 16 histories at forecast time).

selection_score: Primary: mean WIS of log(1 + admissions) over the 50 states and DC, Hub horizons 0-3, October-May reference dates, 2024-25 and 2025-26 equal (main problem), each recipe's deployed view, averaged over seeds 44-51; lower is better. Reported beside it: each season, the 2023-24 guard, October-only, US, ED share (2025-26), interval coverage, pairwise relative WIS against the Hub models (scripts/flu_search_table.py).
anti_overfitting_rules: No 2026-27 data in any training, evaluation or selection step (no live gate).
Eight seeds per recipe from the first screen (44-51); finalists get 16 more seeds (52-67) before any choice.

A child beats its parent only if its primary is lower by more than max(2 x standard error of the difference, 1% of the parent), it is lower in both 2024-25 and 2025-26, and its 2023-24 guard is not worse by more than that margin. Smaller differences are 'level' and are not pursued.
Prefer changes with a mechanism (nowcast, double counting, data, structure) over continuous tuning; no random hyperparameter searches before the structural axes are closed.
An axis is closed after two rounds without a 'better' child. Combinations only of children that were 'better' on their own.
The release candidate is chosen on seed mixtures (each recipe's seeds pooled) of a few recipes, compared with the B7 mixture refit leak-free on the same seeds; mixture weights are equal, never tuned.

Added 20 Nov 17:25 (user concern about peaks): WIS in each state's peak window (target weeks within 2 weeks of its finalized season maximum, 14% of tasks) is reported for every finalist and mixture (scripts/flu_phase_check.py); a candidate may not be worse there by more than the margin, because season-average WIS is dominated by the more numerous falling and rising weeks.

decisions.what: Pulled origin/main (781efed); the local modifications and untracked files were byte-identical to origin, so nothing needed a 'progress' commit (local copies kept in git stash). Study set up: protocol, rounds.py, the 2023-24 guard problem, scripts/flu_search.sbatch, flu_search_score.sbatch, flu_search_table.py, flu_first_week_signal.py.
Round 1: 4 references + 3 roots + 50 one-factor children = 57 recipes x seeds 44-51, main problem (flu-s-r01) then guard (flu-s-g01), one Slurm array over the free lab GPUs.

GBQR member test (scripts/flu_gbqr.py, first version, untuned: sklearn quantile gradient boosting per Hub level, pooled over locations and horizons, trained on finalized 2022-23..2025-26 histories of each fold, inputs = the paired run's tree-corrected Wednesday reports). Paired with T.real of nowcast-tree-20261113-r01 (B_width256 + real-pair trees, error_reference=2025-2026, i.e. the old leaky errors; seeds 44-47). States/DC WIS of log(1 + admissions), 2024-25 / 2025-26 / mean / October-only, lower is better, each a 4-seed equal mixture: network 0.2883 / 0.2846 / 0.2865 / 0.454; GBQR 0.2969 / 0.2713 / 0.2841 / 0.376; equal network+GBQR mixture 0.2755 / 0.2635 / 0.2695 / 0.394 (-6% against the network, lower in both seasons). GBQR intervals are too narrow (50% intervals cover 43%, 90% cover 81-82%); the mixture's cover 50-53% and 88-91%. ED share WIS (natural, states/DC) 0.00502 / 0.00444 network, 0.00494 / 0.00413 mixture. Decision: mixtures with a structurally different learner are the first large, season-consistent gain; GBQR is kept untuned apart from principled variants (pre-2022 ILI augmentation, bagging), paired with the round-1 leaders.

User (20 Nov): does not much like GBQR, prefers trajectories, asks whether it could favour non-peak weeks. Checked by epidemic phase (scripts/flu_phase_check.py; same 4-seed mixtures as the 16:50 entry: network T.real of nowcast-tree-20261113-r01 trained on 2022-23..2025-26 minus the held-out season, GBQR paired with it, and their equal mixture; held-out 2024-25 and 2025-26 archived reports, states/DC, horizons 0-3; phase of the target week from the state's finalized season curve: peak = within 2 weeks of its maximum, 14% of tasks; rising 31%; falling 55%). WIS of log(1 + admissions), network / GBQR / mixture: rising 0.320 / 0.309 / 0.291, peak 0.299 / 0.333 / 0.299, falling 0.255 / 0.251 / 0.242. Near the peak GBQR is worse, lower (bias log(median/truth) -0.36 against -0.30) and overconfident (50% intervals cover 23% against 34%); in 2024-25's sharp peak 0.391 against 0.313, and the mixture 0.331 is worse than the network alone. Every model is far too low near the peak (bias -0.57 to -0.66 at horizon 3). So GBQR's gain is off-peak, where most tasks lie, which is why season-average WIS (and Hub rankings) favour it. GBQR with pre-2022 ILI rows (weight 0.5) is worse alone (0.2922 against 0.2841). Decisions: GBQR is not a release candidate (marginal quantiles, no trajectories, poor at peaks); the gain from structural diversity is pursued among sampled (trajectory) networks instead; peak-window WIS is added as a guard: a child or mixture may not be worse near the peak by more than the margin.
